separate.question: How is the grading system structured?
separate.answer:
**Grading system structure for each online programme** | Programme | Internal evaluation | Final University examination | Grading conversion | |-----------|---------------------|------------------------------|--------------------| | **Online MCA** | 30 % of the course marks | 70 % of the course marks (written paper, practical, oral, presentation or any combination) | Total marks are converted to a letter grade on a ten‑point scale (exact ranges not shown in the excerpt). | | **Online BCA** | 50 % of the course marks (continuous assessment, practical, oral, presentation or any combination) | 50 % of the course marks (written paper, practical, oral, presentation or any combination) | A grade other than **F** or **Ab** is required to earn credit; passing marks are 36 % overall. | | **Online BBA** | 30 % of the course marks (continuous assessment) | 70 % of the course marks (written paper, practical, oral, presentation or any combination) | Letter grades and grade points are assigned as follows:
• ≥ 96 % → **O** (10)
• 86–94 % → **A+** (9)
• 76–85 % → **A** (8)
• 66–75 % → **B+** (7)
• 56–65 % → **B** (6)
• 46–55 % → **C** (5)
• 36–45 % → **P** (4)
• < 35 % → **F** (0) | | **Online MBA** | Internal marks + final University marks are combined | Combined marks are converted to a letter grade on a ten‑point scale (exact ranges not provided in the excerpt). | | *The grading structure is consistent across programmes: internal assessment contributes a set percentage of the course marks
